opening.text: Think about the day a child learns to tie a shoe. The parent shows the loop. The child tries and it falls apart. The parent shows it again. And again. It takes many tries and a lot of patience. Then one morning, the child ties the shoes alone and looks up with a big smile.
Teaching the gospel to children works the same way. It is a small lesson, repeated with love, over many days. Let us look at how it is done.

mainMessage.text: Parents are the first and most important teachers of the gospel. We teach in small, steady ways, we do it in our homes, and we point our children to Jesus Christ. God helps us as we try.

blocks.text: **Home is where the lessons live.** A child learns to tie shoes at home, not in a classroom. The home is also the best place to learn about God. It is where children see faith in daily life.
But I have commanded you to bring up your children in light and truth.

Brother Tad R. Callister, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Parents: The Prime Gospel Teachers of Their Children” from the October 2014 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
When all is said and done, the home is the ideal forum for teaching the gospel of Jesus Christ.
The home is where it happens.

**Teach as the moments come.** A parent does not schedule shoe-tying lessons. They happen when the child is ready. Gospel moments come the same way, at the table, in the car or at bedtime. We can be ready for them.
And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
We always need to be ready to teach our children because we never know when the opportunity will present itself.
We watch for the moment.

**Show the loops in the scriptures.** A child needs to see the loop again and again. Scripture study at home shows them what it looks like to follow Christ. It can be short. It can be simple. But it can be steady.

Angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost; wherefore, they speak the words of Christ. Wherefore, I said unto you, feast upon the words of Christ; for behold, the words of Christ will tell you all things what ye should do.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Family scripture study is an ideal forum for teaching doctrine in the home.
A few verses a day add up.

**Start each day with the same step.** Tying a shoe is the same motion each time. A family habit can be that simple. Morning prayer is one of the best. It teaches children to begin their day with God.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.

Brother Tad R. Callister, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Parents: The Prime Gospel Teachers of Their Children” from the October 2014 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
As parents, we can help instill within our children the habit and power of morning prayer.
A simple habit becomes a strength.

**Introduce them to the One who loves them.** The most important thing a parent teaches is who God is. Children who know their Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ have a firm place to stand. Parents are the ones who make that first introduction.

And we talk of Christ, we rejoice in Christ, we preach of Christ, we prophesy of Christ, and we write according to our prophecies, that our children may know to what source they may look for a remission of their sins.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
As parents, we introduce our children to Heavenly Father and His Son, Jesus Christ.
We help them meet the Savior.
**Tie your own shoes where they can see.** Children learn by watching. They see how we treat each other and how we pray. A home where parents love each other and live the gospel is itself a lesson.
And they shall also teach their children to pray, and to walk uprightly before the Lord.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
As parents cherish each other and offer righteous examples, children are eternally blessed.
Our example teaches more than our words.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they taught a child, or when someone taught them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jesus Blesses the Little Children

blocks.text: Jesus took the Nephite children one by one and blessed them. Then He invited their parents to see them. He showed how much He cared for each child.

And when he had said these words, he wept, and the multitude bare record of it, and he took their little children, one by one, and blessed them, and prayed unto the Father for them. And he spake unto the multitude, and said unto them: Behold your little ones.
The Savior sees each child. We can learn to do the same.

application.text: First, pick one small gospel habit to teach a child this week, such as a morning prayer or a verse at dinner.
Second, watch for one unplanned moment to teach. When it comes, say a short, kind word about God.
Third, let a child see you pray or read the scriptures. If you need help as a parent, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God cares about every child. I know that He helps parents and teachers who try. I have seen how small, steady teaching can shape a life. I know that Jesus Christ loves the children and blesses them. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A young vine has plenty of energy, but it has no idea where to go. Left alone, it sprawls on the ground. Give it a trellis, and it climbs toward the sun. The trellis does not force the vine to grow. It gives the vine something to hold on to.
Parents can be a trellis for their children. We do not make them grow. We give them something strong to hold. Let us see how.

mainMessage.text: Children grow best with steady support and a clear direction. Parents give both. We teach the gospel at home, we point to Christ and we live what we teach.

blocks.text: **The garden is the home.** A trellis stands in a garden, not in a store. The home is where children are raised in light and truth. It is the best classroom the gospel has.
But I have commanded you to bring up your children in light and truth.

Brother Tad R. Callister, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Parents: The Prime Gospel Teachers of Their Children” from the October 2014 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
When all is said and done, the home is the ideal forum for teaching the gospel of Jesus Christ.
The garden is at home.

**Be ready when the vine reaches.** A vine reaches suddenly. A child asks a big question at an odd time. A good gardener is ready with something to hold. A good parent is ready with a kind, simple answer.
And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
We always need to be ready to teach our children because we never know when the opportunity will present itself.
We keep the trellis ready.
**Build the trellis from scripture.** A trellis needs strong wood. The scriptures are strong wood. When a family studies them together, the children have something firm to climb.

Angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost; wherefore, they speak the words of Christ. Wherefore, I said unto you, feast upon the words of Christ; for behold, the words of Christ will tell you all things what ye should do.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Family scripture study is an ideal forum for teaching doctrine in the home.
Strong wood holds the vine.
**Morning sun.** A vine turns to the light each morning. A child can learn to turn to God at the start of each day. Morning prayer is a simple way to do it.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.

Brother Tad R. Callister, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Parents: The Prime Gospel Teachers of Their Children” from the October 2014 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
As parents, we can help instill within our children the habit and power of morning prayer.
The day begins turned toward the light.
**Reach toward the Light.** The vine climbs to reach the sun. Our children climb to know the Savior. Parents are the ones who point up and say, “There He is.”

And we talk of Christ, we rejoice in Christ, we preach of Christ, we prophesy of Christ, and we write according to our prophecies, that our children may know to what source they may look for a remission of their sins.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
As parents, we introduce our children to Heavenly Father and His Son, Jesus Christ.
We point them to the Light.
**Strong posts hold the trellis.** A trellis stands on firm posts. For our children, parents are the posts. When we cherish each other and live the gospel, they stand on something solid.
And they shall also teach their children to pray, and to walk uprightly before the Lord.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
As parents cherish each other and offer righteous examples, children are eternally blessed.
Our example is the post.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a child learned something from their example. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Young Samuel Learns to Listen

blocks.text: Samuel was a young boy serving in the temple. When the Lord called, he did not know who was speaking. Eli taught him how to answer.

Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place. And the Lord came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.
Eli gave Samuel a simple thing to hold. A child learned to listen to the Lord.

application.text: First, think of one child you can help. Write down one simple way to give them something strong to hold.
Second, share one scripture or story with them this week. Keep it short.
Third, let them see you turn to God in prayer. If you feel unsure as a parent or teacher, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that children are precious to God. I know that He helps us support them. I have felt joy in seeing a child reach for the Savior. I know that Jesus Christ blesses those who teach with love. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

versions.analogy: A trellis for a young vine

opening.text: It is bedtime. The house is quiet and a small lamp is on. A child is tucked in, eyes getting heavy. A parent sits on the edge of the bed and tells a story. These minutes are small, but children remember them for the rest of their lives.
Some of the best teaching happens in moments like these. Let us look at how parents can use them.

mainMessage.text: Children learn the gospel best when they feel safe and loved. Parents do not need a perfect lesson. They need a warm lamp, a few simple words and the habit of coming back every day.

blocks.text: **Where the lamp is warm.** A child falls asleep best where the light is soft and the voice is kind. The home is where that happens. It is the best place for the gospel to be taught.
But I have commanded you to bring up your children in light and truth.

Brother Tad R. Callister, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Parents: The Prime Gospel Teachers of Their Children” from the October 2014 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
When all is said and done, the home is the ideal forum for teaching the gospel of Jesus Christ.
The warmest lamp is at home.

**The question you did not plan for.** A child, nearly asleep, asks a deep question. “Where was I before I was born?” Those moments come without warning. A parent who is ready can give a gentle, honest answer.
And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
We always need to be ready to teach our children because we never know when the opportunity will present itself.
We stay ready for the quiet question.
**One page a night.** A bedtime story does not have to be long. One page is enough. A few verses of scripture each night, shared together, can teach a child what matters most.

Angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost; wherefore, they speak the words of Christ. Wherefore, I said unto you, feast upon the words of Christ; for behold, the words of Christ will tell you all things what ye should do.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Family scripture study is an ideal forum for teaching doctrine in the home.
A page a night adds up.
**Wake up with a prayer.** The lamp goes off at night, and the sun comes up in the morning. A short morning prayer can be the start of a good day. Children learn to turn to God first.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.

Brother Tad R. Callister, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Parents: The Prime Gospel Teachers of Their Children” from the October 2014 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
As parents, we can help instill within our children the habit and power of morning prayer.
A good habit holds a whole day.

**A story about a Friend.** The best bedtime stories are about someone we love. Parents can tell their children about the Savior as a real person and a real friend. Over time, the child comes to know Him.

And we talk of Christ, we rejoice in Christ, we preach of Christ, we prophesy of Christ, and we write according to our prophecies, that our children may know to what source they may look for a remission of their sins.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
As parents, we introduce our children to Heavenly Father and His Son, Jesus Christ.
We help them know the Savior.

**The story they see you live.** Children also watch what happens when the lamp is off. They see how their parents speak to each other and how they handle a hard day. That story teaches even more than words.
And they shall also teach their children to pray, and to walk uprightly before the Lord.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
As parents cherish each other and offer righteous examples, children are eternally blessed.
The life we live tells the story.

story.title: Jesus Welcomes the Children

blocks.text: Parents brought their children to Jesus. His disciples tried to send them away. The Savior welcomed them instead.

But when he saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God. And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.
The Savior opens His arms to every child. Parents can help bring them there.

application.text: First, pick one quiet time this week to sit with a child. Tell them one thing you believe about God.
Second, read one short scripture story together at bedtime.
Third, thank the child for something they did well that day. If you need help as a parent, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that quiet moments can carry great meaning. I know that the Savior loves the children and wants them close. I have felt Him near when I taught a child. I know that He helps every parent who tries. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Before a concert, every musician in the orchestra tunes. One note from the oboe, and the whole room settles into it. A small act, done first, shapes everything that follows.
Parents can help their children tune each day. It does not take long. But it can set the tone for everything. Let us see how.

mainMessage.text: Teaching children is like helping them learn an instrument. It takes daily practice, a patient guide and a good example. And the music is the sound of a family following Christ.

blocks.text: **Practice in the home room.** Musicians practice at home before they perform. The home is the best place for children to learn the gospel. It is where they can practice with people who love them.
But I have commanded you to bring up your children in light and truth.

And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.

Brother Tad R. Callister, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Parents: The Prime Gospel Teachers of Their Children” from the October 2014 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).

And they shall also teach their children to pray, and to walk uprightly before the Lord.

Brother Devin G. Durrant, First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency, said this in his talk “Teaching in the Home—a Joyful and Sacred Responsibility” from the April 2018 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a parent or teacher gave them a lasting lesson. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Alma Encourages His Son Shiblon

blocks.text: Alma wrote to his son Shiblon with love. He did not scold him. He praised his steadiness and encouraged him to keep going.

And now, my son, I trust that I shall have great joy in you, because of your steadiness and your faithfulness unto God; for as you have commenced in your youth to look to the Lord your God, even so I hope that you will continue in keeping his commandments; for blessed is he that endureth to the end.
A parent’s encouragement can carry a child for years.

application.text: First, choose one daily “tuning” habit for your family, such as a short morning prayer.
Second, tell a child one thing you admire about them, the way Alma did for Shiblon.
Third, play the melody you want them to learn. Let them see you pray or read. If you need help, speak with your bishop or branch president.

Parents make the most important introduction there is. They introduce their children to God. Let us look at how that is done.

mainMessage.text: The heart of teaching children is helping them know their Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ. We do it with simple words, steady habits and our own example. The Lord helps us do it.

blocks.text: **The party is at home.** The first introductions happen close to home, at the table, by the door or on the couch. The home is where children first meet God. It is the best place for it.
But I have commanded you to bring up your children in light and truth.

Brother Tad R. Callister, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Parents: The Prime Gospel Teachers of Their Children” from the October 2014 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).

And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone helped them know God, or when they helped a child know Him. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Helaman Gives His Sons Names to Remember

blocks.text: Helaman named his sons Nephi and Lehi. He wanted them to remember the good people who came before them. He taught them to live up to the name.

Behold, my sons, I desire that ye should remember to keep the commandments of God; and I would that ye should declare unto the people these words. Behold, I have given unto you the names of our first parents who came out of the land of Jerusalem; and this I have done that when you remember your names ye may remember them; and when ye remember them ye may remember their works; and when ye remember their works ye may know how that it is said, and also written, that they were good. Therefore, my sons, I would that ye should do that which is good, that it may be said of you, and also written, even as it has been said and written of them.
Helaman helped his sons know good examples. That is part of a good introduction.

application.text: First, think of a child you love. Write down one thing you want them to know about God.
Second, tell them that this week, in a simple way.
Third, share one example of a good person who helped you know God. If you need help as a parent or teacher, speak with your bishop or branch president.
